elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
elements.evidence: Revised 13.2: "Ono shall have the right to terminate this Agreement for convenience at any time, for any reasons..." This is a licence/development agreement with no Order Form construct, so an Agreement-level right is the full scope available; the deterministic check "Customer convenience termination present: false" is a false negative against the rendered text, which expressly grants the convenience right to Ono (Customer).

elements.element: Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.
elements.evidence: "by giving thirty (30) days' advance written notice to Array" — the redacted "[ * ] advance written notice" is replaced with a fixed 30-day figure. The retained requirement that the notice be "accompanied by the rationale for such termination" is a formality carried over from the original, not an added condition precedent beyond notice.

elements.element: Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.
elements.evidence: "Array shall refund to Ono on a pro rata basis any fees prepaid by Ono for the period after the effective date of such termination." The refund is expressly pro rata (not merely post-termination-period), runs from Vendor to Customer, and is tied to convenience termination under 13.2.

elements.element: Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
elements.evidence: Array's termination rights in the cited text are limited to material breach with cure (13.3), plus (per the finding) bankruptcy (13.4) and the Section 8.2 Competing Product breach; 13.5(a) grants Safety/Efficacy termination to Ono alone. None is an at-will/convenience exit, so no carve-out edit is needed and the element is already satisfied. Note: 13.4 and the 13.5 lead-in are not reproduced in the rendered excerpt, so this rests on the drafter's cited review of Article 13, but nothing in the excerpt contradicts it.

elements.element: Customer may terminate for convenience on 60 to 90 days' notice.
elements.evidence: Notice is fixed at "thirty (30) days'" in revised 13.2, which is below the 60–90 day fallback band. This is intentional (the preferred position is stronger for us) and does not defeat position-completeness at the preferred level.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: revised 13.2 imposes no early-termination fee, penalty or contingent payment on Ono for exercising the convenience right, so there is no fee to cap. Section 6.1's non-refundable upfront licence fee is a pre-existing consideration term, not an exit fee triggered by termination.

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply and is exceeded: Array has no convenience termination right at all (only material breach under 13.3, plus bankruptcy and the 8.2 Competing Product route), which is stronger than an end-of-term-only right.

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 90 days' notice of convenience termination.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: with no Array convenience right anywhere in Article 13, there is no Vendor convenience notice period to set. Array's breach termination under 13.3 already runs on a 90-day cure/notice cycle.

reasons: Position-complete at the preferred level: all four preferred elements are met in operative language (convenience right at any time, 30 days' written notice, express pro rata refund of prepaid fees for the post-termination period, and no Array convenience right).

The deterministic check "Customer convenience termination present: false" is a mechanical false negative; substantively, revised 13.2 reads "Ono shall have the right to terminate this Agreement for convenience at any time... by giving thirty (30) days' advance written notice," which satisfies the pattern's intent. No repair is required, though the drafter may wish to confirm the detector is keyed to the clause heading "Termination by Ono without Cause" rather than the body text.

Minimal: the edit touches only 13.2, deleting the commencement trigger that blocked the exit until a redacted period after First Commercial Sale of both Products (necessary to reach element 1), fixing the redacted notice figure at 30 days (element 2) and adding a single refund sentence (element 3). It retains "for any reasons" and the rationale formality verbatim, and leaves 13.1, 13.3, 13.4 and 13.5 untouched. Correctly omits the model language's "in whole or in part," which is surplus absent an Order Form or partial-termination structure here.

Preserves intent: the refund is limited to period-allocated prepayments, so it does not contradict the retained non-refundable upfront licence fee in 6.1; the breach, bankruptcy, Safety and Efficacy termination routes and the Section 13.1 post-expiry perpetual licence survive unchanged, with no dangling cross-reference or undefined term created.

Downstream point correctly quarantined rather than fixed here: the Section 8.2 Competing Product post-termination tail keyed to an at-will exit during the Initial Royalty Term can now be triggered earlier. That is a consequence of the (necessary) removal of the commencement trigger, not an internal contradiction in 13.2, and belongs in a separate 8.2 finding as the rationale states — folding it into this redline would fail minimality.

Fallback is not satisfied (30-day notice sits below the 60–90 day band), but that is irrelevant to completeness because the preferred checklist is fully met; the margin comment appropriately offers 60–90 days as the negotiation retreat without conceding it in operative text.
